scope_compliance_statement: This file defines the contract for how the player interacts with world objects and characters. It contains no mission triggers, no dialogue text, no minigame implementation, and no lockpick/hacking mechanics — only the stub interfaces future packages implement against.

contract.target_actor_reference: An interactable may optionally reference a character_id from CharacterFramework's CharacterRegistry (CHAR_ prefix) if the interactable is a character rather than a static object — e.g. approaching CHAR_echo for a conversation trigger.
contract.content_policy: This contract defines that an object CAN be interacted with. It does not define what happens narratively when it is — that belongs to a future Missions or Dialogue package.

contract.player_dependency: Reads the active player's InputActionMappingContract (PlayerFramework, EP-PLAYER-02) 'interaction_trigger' abstract action category to know which input fires the prompt.
contract.ui_policy: UI-agnostic — this contract fires an event; it does not define prompt visuals, text, or placement.

contract.fires_on: successful interactable_object_contract resolution where the target is a character_id
contract.payload: character_id and interactable_id only — no dialogue content, no line of text, no conversation state.
contract.consumer: A future Dialogue package subscribes to this event; this framework has no knowledge of what that package does with it.
contract.example_non_content: This stub could fire for an interaction with CHAR_echo. It does not know or care that Echo's first words are 'Hello? Is someone there? I remember...' — that content lives entirely in the locked Meridian_Master package and any future Dialogue package, never here.

confirmed_world_examples_referenced_not_: Metro Archives' sealed exhibit case lockpick minigame (Metro_Archives.md Sec. 8.2, locked Meridian_Master package)
Undercroft/Metro Archives hacking-deck interactions (Vol I, 7.2, locked canon)
contract.content_policy: This framework does not implement lockpicking or hacking mechanics. It only guarantees a stub interface exists for a future package to attach that implementation to.

canon_references.usage: Justifies that dialogue_trigger_stub must support targeting a non-corporeal character_id (CHAR_echo) the same way it supports a physical one.

interaction_execution_model.added_during: Phase 2 audit — the new brief requires this explicit flow, which was previously only implicit across the four contracts above.
interaction_execution_model.flow: PLAYER -> INTERACTION_REQUEST -> TARGET -> VALIDATION -> ACTION -> RESULT -> WORLD_OR_GAMEPLAY_STATE_CHANGE
interaction_execution_model.validation_step: Checks interaction_range and any interactable-specific preconditions (e.g. minigame_required flag) before ACTION executes. Not previously named as a distinct step in this file.

failure_states.confirmed: minigame_interaction_stub's success/failure callback is the one explicit failure-capable interaction type.
failure_states.undefined_remainder: General interaction failure (e.g. a failed dialogue check, a failed environmental exploit) has no confirmed consequence model — UNDEFINED — IMPLEMENTATION DECISION REQUIRED.

system_events.consumed_by: Future AI package (for NPC awareness) and future Missions package (for objective tracking) — this framework only emits; it does not define consumers' reactions.

persistence_implications.pointer: SaveFramework.json's PersistentStateRegistry already registers SAVE_interaction_completion_state for exactly this purpose.
